title: Fire Emblem's Crossover With Shin Megami Tensei Became an Idol RPG
hook:
In 2013 Nintendo announced a Fire Emblem and Shin Megami Tensei crossover, then it vanished for two years and came back as a game about pop idols in modern Tokyo. Would you play a Fire Emblem idol game?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the Fire Emblem crossover with Shin Megami Tensei turned into a game about pop idols? In January of two thousand thirteen, a Nintendo Direct announced a Wii U game called Shin Megami Tensei X Fire Emblem. The teaser showed nothing but characters from both series and a title. Atlus would build it with help from Intelligent Systems, the studio behind Fire Emblem. Then the game vanished for more than two years. When it returned in April of two thousand fifteen, it looked nothing like that teaser. Fire Emblem heroes like Chrom were now Mirages, spirit allies who had lost their memories. They fought beside teenagers in modern Tokyo chasing careers in music, acting and modeling. Nintendo producer Hitoshi Yamagami later said the first plan was a strategy game. About six months in, the team changed direction to play to the strengths of Atlus. Atlus producer Shinjiro Takada said they picked the entertainment industry to set it apart from other RPGs. The idol songs came from the Japanese music giant Avex. Japan got the game first, in December of 2015, under a different name. The West got it as Tokyo Mirage Sessions FE in June of 2016. A Switch version called Encore followed in January of 2020. Follow for more gaming history.
